label: Early original-phase steps shortly after e/g/y/x/t/r
explanation: Fires during the first few original-input steps (t=1..4, peaking at t=2-3; never at t=0, rare after t=5, nearly silent in the copy phase) when one of the tokens e, g, y, x, t, r appeared one or two steps earlier. The current input token barely matters. e is the strongest trigger (prev_tok rate 0.42), then g and y. Magnitude is largest when triggers repeat: the top activations (about 1.0) all come from sequences starting e e, at t=3. Coverage rises with activation quartile (0.56 in the lowest quartile, 0.96 in the highest), so the weak activations not captured are a diffuse tail: a few delimiter-step firings (3% of mass), t=5 firings, and firings after other tokens such as q or h. It does not fire later in long sequences even when trigger tokens appear, and it does not fire in the copy phase.

issues: Minor: the explanation says the feature fires at t=1..4, but t=5 still has an 8.1% firing rate and 4.8% of the activation mass. Extending the predicate to t<=5 raises recall to 0.86 but drops precision to 0.733 (F1 0.792), so cutting off at t<=4 is the right trade-off.

Minor: inside the predicate, the case where the trigger is only two steps back is weaker. Precision is 0.715 overall for it and 0.53 at t=4. Firing when the trigger is the previous token is the core (precision 0.89).

Misses on the test split (12.4% of mass) are a scattered tail at t=5-7, a trigger three steps back, q/h/3, and the delimiter. I found no single systematic class: adding rel_tok(-3), seen(), or q/h/3 to the predicate all lowered F1 (0.74-0.78).

Factual claims checked out on the profile. t=0 rate is 0. Copy phase has 0.1% of mass and delimiter 3.1%. prev_tok=e rate is 0.418, with g at 0.395 and y at 0.379. Top activations are about 1.0 at t=3 after 'e e'. Coverage by quartile goes 0.56/0.80/0.91/0.96. in_tok rates are flat (0.10-0.12).
Test scores reproduce: P 0.825, R 0.809, F1 0.817, mass recall 0.876.
